# Example Winsteps output

`pfile_example.out` is a genuine `PFILE=` written by Winsteps on Windows,
kept so that the parsing in `winsteps_read_person_output()` is tested against
the real layout rather than a reconstruction of it. It shows the details that
are easy to get wrong from documentation alone: the leading comment line, the
column-name line commented out with `;` (so the first name arrives as
`;ENTRY`), values written without a leading zero (`.72`, not `0.72`), and a
trailing blank line.

**The measures in it are not a valid estimation.** It came from the W2 probe,
which fed Winsteps a deliberately malformed data file -- a response block wider
than `NI` declared -- to confirm that Winsteps accepts such a file silently.
Use this file for format, never as an example of what a correct run produces.


## Example run set

`example_responses.csv` and `example_anchors.csv` are the inputs to a worked
example: 200 persons, 12 items in two interleaved domains of six, 25 genuinely missing
responses, and persons at both score extremes. Responses are simulated from
the Rasch model using the same difficulties that then serve as anchors, so an
anchored run against this data is a well-fitting one and displacement should
sit near zero -- which is what makes it usable as an example of anchors being
applied correctly.

The domains alternate rather than splitting the item list down the middle. A
domain made only of the six easiest items is answered correctly by almost
everyone, so a domain run against it returns a mass of perfect scores and
demonstrates nothing; alternating keeps both domains spanning the full
difficulty range.

The sample size is deliberate: displacement must be read against the standard
error of the item measure, which is about half a logit at 30 persons and about
0.15 at 200. A first run at 30 persons produced displacements of several
tenths on a perfectly anchored run, which would have taught the wrong lesson.

Both files are generated by `data-raw/make_example_data.R`. The Winsteps output
for them is produced by `data-raw/make_example_run.R`, which must be run on
Windows.

## Output from a real run

`example_domain1_person.out`, `example_domain1_item.out` and
`example_domain1_delete.txt` are genuine Winsteps output for the example data
above, from an anchored run restricted to domain 1 (`q01`, `q03`, `q05`, `q07`,
`q09`, `q11`). Unlike `pfile_example.out`, this is a **correct** run and its
measures can be shown as such.

Two things in the item file are worth knowing, and neither is obvious from the
Winsteps documentation:

- Item names come back as `q01`, `q03`, ... rather than `I0001`, `I0002`, ...
  only because the names are written as labels after `&END`. Winsteps treats
  the names in the anchor file as comments and never reads them.
- `ENTRY` keeps the sequence numbers from the full item bank (1, 3, 5, 7, 9,
  11) rather than renumbering the six retained items 1-6, so item output from a
  subset run joins back to the bank on either `ENTRY` or `NAME`.

`MEASURE` equals the supplied anchor value exactly, and `DISPL` -- the gap
between the anchor and what the data implies -- stays under half a logit. That
is the picture a correctly anchored run should present.
